meta_desc: Step-by-step NCERT Class 12 Exercise 7.11 solutions on properties of definite integrals, plus a free 8-question quiz on the king property and symmetry.

quiz.title: Properties of Definite Integrals Quiz
quiz.intro: Eight questions on the properties used all through Exercise 7.11 — the king property, even and odd functions over symmetric limits, and the 0 to 2a split. Pick an answer, then press Check my score.

questions.q: The 'king property' states that the integral of f(x) from 0 to a equals the integral from 0 to a of which function?
questions.explanation: Substituting x → a − x leaves the limits 0 and a unchanged and gives ∫<sub>0</sub><sup>a</sup> f(x) dx = ∫<sub>0</sub><sup>a</sup> f(a − x) dx.

questions.q: If f is an odd function, the integral of f(x) from −a to a equals:
questions.explanation: For an odd function f(−x) = −f(x), the areas on either side of 0 cancel, so the integral over the symmetric interval [−a, a] is 0.

questions.q: If f is an even function, the integral of f(x) from −a to a equals:
questions.explanation: For an even function f(−x) = f(x), the two halves are equal, so ∫<sub>−a</sub><sup>a</sup> f(x) dx = 2∫<sub>0</sub><sup>a</sup> f(x) dx.

questions.q: Using the king property, ∫<sub>0</sub><sup>π/2</sup> sin x / (sin x + cos x) dx equals:
questions.explanation: Call the integral I. Applying x → π/2 − x gives I = ∫ cos x/(cos x + sin x) dx. Adding the two forms, 2I = ∫<sub>0</sub><sup>π/2</sup> 1 dx = π/2, so I = π/4.

questions.q: The integral of x³ from −2 to 2 is:
questions.explanation: x³ is an odd function and the limits are symmetric about 0, so the integral is 0 without any further calculation.

questions.q: ∫<sub>0</sub><sup>2a</sup> f(x) dx can be written as which of the following?
questions.explanation: Splitting at a and substituting x → 2a − x in the second piece gives ∫<sub>0</sub><sup>2a</sup> f(x) dx = ∫<sub>0</sub><sup>a</sup> [f(x) + f(2a − x)] dx.

questions.q: By the 0 to 2a rule, ∫<sub>0</sub><sup>2a</sup> f(x) dx = 2∫<sub>0</sub><sup>a</sup> f(x) dx holds when:
questions.explanation: When f(2a − x) = f(x) the second piece equals the first, doubling the 0-to-a integral; if instead f(2a − x) = −f(x) the result is 0.

questions.q: The integral of cos x from −π/2 to π/2 is:
questions.explanation: cos x is even, so ∫<sub>−π/2</sub><sup>π/2</sup> cos x dx = 2∫<sub>0</sub><sup>π/2</sup> cos x dx = 2[sin x]<sub>0</sub><sup>π/2</sup> = 2(1 − 0) = 2.

faq.q: What does Exercise 7.11 of NCERT Class 12 Maths cover?
faq.a: Exercise 7.11 is on the properties of definite integrals. The problems use the king property ∫<sub>0</sub><sup>a</sup> f(x) dx = ∫<sub>0</sub><sup>a</sup> f(a − x) dx, the even and odd function rules over symmetric limits, and the 0-to-2a split to evaluate integrals that are hard to compute directly.

faq.q: What is the king property of definite integrals?
faq.a: The king property says ∫<sub>0</sub><sup>a</sup> f(x) dx = ∫<sub>0</sub><sup>a</sup> f(a − x) dx, and more generally ∫<sub>b</sub><sup>a</sup> f(x) dx = ∫<sub>b</sub><sup>a</sup> f(a + b − x) dx. It replaces x by the reflected value, and adding the original and reflected integrals often collapses a messy expression into a simple constant.

faq.q: How do even and odd functions simplify a symmetric integral?
faq.a: Over a symmetric interval [−a, a], an odd function integrates to 0 because the two halves cancel, while an even function integrates to twice the 0-to-a integral. Spotting the symmetry first can save an entire page of working.

faq.q: Why do so many trigonometric integrals appear in this exercise?
faq.a: Ratios like sin x/(sin x + cos x) on [0, π/2] are the classic testing ground for the king property. The substitution x → π/2 − x swaps sine and cosine, so adding the two forms gives 2I = a constant — a trick that recurs in board and JEE papers.
